mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5.25% for two consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains elevated for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the prior 20-day window with similar FEDFUNDS levels (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in the Consumer Price Index exceeds +0.5% in a month following a negative core inflation surprise, it signals a shift toward price stability that boosts investor confidence and drives S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly change > +0.5% and previous month's core CPI surprise < -0.2%
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no significant deviation from the mean of prior 60-day windows with similar CPIAUCSL changes (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in employment growth (PAYEMS) by more than 20,000 jobs in a single month coincides with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5%, creating a pro-labor economic momentum that is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >20,000 and UNRATE falls below 3.5% in the same month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative despite the labor indicators meeting or exceeding the trigger thresholds (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly industrial production index (INDPRO) below 101 combined with a 2% decline in the S&P 500's own production (not in catalog, so use proxy: GDPC1) suggests weakening manufacturing momentum that depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the prior 20-day window with similar INDPRO and GDPC1 levels (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When personal consumption expenditures (proxy: GDPC1) grow at a monthly rate exceeding 2% in a month where retail sales (not in catalog - skip) or housing starts (not in catalog - skip) are missing, the signal of strong consumer demand is inferred and is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly change > +2% and no available retail/housing proxies to contradict
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no significant positive deviation from a neutral baseline (mean of prior 60-day windows) (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3% for three consecutive months, without a corresponding rise in inflation (CPIAUCSL), indicates a tight labor market that the Fed is likely to respond to by raising rates, which should produce negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 3% for three consecutive months and CPIAUCSL change < +0.3% in the same period
regime_hint: labor market tightness without inflationary pressure
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative relative to the prior 20-day window with similar UNRATE/CPIAUCSL (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of declining consumer prices (CPIAUCSL < 305) and rising wage growth (PAYEMS), a 1% increase in monthly pay growth outperforms inflation, signaling wage-driven inflation and eroding real earnings, which should be associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically negative when compared to the prior 5-day window with similar PAYEMS/CPIAUCSL (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A two consecutive months of industrial production (INDPRO) below 102 with no recovery in manufacturing momentum (no proxy in catalog) suggests a supply-side shock that persists into the next quarter, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than the prior 60-day window with similar INDPRO levels (p > 0.10).
